reason: Feed the inner swarm to advance the rocky-world goal.
expectation: The added pebbles may make the rocky swarm dense enough to begin forming a larger body, though the immediate result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The outer swarm also needs pebbles, but I chose to follow the inner swarm first.

effect: The inner swarm has collapsed into many separate rocky bodies, which can now encounter other stones or impactors.
reaction: The transition from loose pebbles to a population of bodies is satisfying.
reason: Gently converging stones seem a promising way to grow one of the rocky bodies.
expectation: Some stones may join the rocky bodies and produce a larger gathering, though the precise result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The icy swarm also needs attention, but I want to follow the rocky bodies first.
Fast impacts could reveal a different outcome, but gentle encounters seem more conducive to growth.

effect: Gentle encounters produced a gravitationally bound loose aggregate, which can now meet the remaining rocky population.
reaction: I like the distinction between an aggregate and a solid monolith.
reason: Combine the aggregate with the rocky population to continue following its growth.
expectation: The aggregate may gather more rocky material into a larger body, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Fast impacts could show a contrasting outcome, but I want to follow the aggregate first.

effect: The aggregate has grown into a larger bound rocky body through a slow encounter.
reaction: The gradual growth makes physical sense, though this step feels similar to the previous one.
reason: Feed the icy swarm to advance the colder-region goal.
expectation: The added pebbles may concentrate into icy bodies, perhaps by gravitational collapse like the rocky swarm.

alternatives.reason: Fast impacts could reveal a contrasting rocky outcome, but the colder-region goal still needs attention.

effect: The outer swarm has collapsed into separate icy bodies that can follow different paths.
reaction: The parallel with the rocky swarm is clear, though somewhat repetitive.
reason: Feed the icy bodies more pebbles to pursue the substantial cold-region body.
expectation: Some icy bodies may grow by gathering pebbles, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Fast rocky impacts could show a contrasting outcome, but I want to continue the icy branch first.

effect: The icy body has grown substantially and completed the colder-region goal; the rocky-world goal remains.
reaction: Its future interaction with disk gas is intriguing.
reason: Fast impacts are the only offered combination and may advance the remaining rocky-world goal.
expectation: The impactors may break or alter some rocky bodies; the exact outcome is uncertain.

effect: A fast impact shattered a separate rocky body, leaving fragments that can now meet the larger body.
reaction: The contrast with the gentle growth encounters is clear.
reason: The only offered combination may incorporate the fragments into the growing rocky body.
expectation: The larger body may gather some fragments and grow, though their encounter could have another outcome.

effect: Fragments from the shattered body enlarged and heated the rocky survivor, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The destructive and constructive paths coming together is satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing fragments from a destructive impact onto the larger survivor tied the two rocky paths together and showed that impacts can both lose and add material.

leastWorthwhile.text: Growing the loose aggregate through another slow encounter felt similar to the preceding gentle-growth step.

surprise.text: The rocky swarm became a population of separate bodies through gravitational collapse rather than simply sticking into one object.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt notably arbitrary; the final fragment combination was the only offered action, but its purpose was clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the large ice-and-rock body's mass affects its interaction with disk gas.
